name: LLM teacher distillation / pseudo-labeling with reversal-consistency filter
links: Task page and rules (LLMs allowed, prompts must be documented): https://inigolopezgazpio.net/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI/ ; LLM annotation evidence: Wang et al. 2021 'Want To Reduce Labeling Cost? GPT-3 Can Help' (arXiv:2108.13487), Gilardi et al. 2023 'ChatGPT outperforms crowd workers for text-annotation tasks' (arXiv:2303.15056) ; generation + filtering for NLI: WANLI (Liu et al. 2022, arXiv:2201.05955) ; critic-filtered distillation: Symbolic Knowledge Distillation (West et al. 2022, arXiv:2110.07178) ; self-training: Noisy Student (Xie et al. 2020, arXiv:1911.04252) ; rationale distillation: Distilling step-by-step (Hsieh et al. 2023, arXiv:2305.02301) ; consistency of LMs: BECEL (Jang et al. COLING 2022) ; Basque teacher: Latxa (Etxaniz et al. 2024, arXiv:2403.20266, HF HiTZ/Latxa-*) ; pilot: https://lrec.elra.info/lrec2026-main-423 . In-repo anchor for the filter: src/labels.py reverse_label / REVERSE_PERM.
license_access: Teacher can be API/closed (Claude, GPT, Gemini: commercial API, terms generally allow using outputs to train non-competing small classifiers but check each ToS) or open-weight (Qwen3, Llama 3.x, Gemma 3, Latxa 3.1 for Basque). The distilled student stays open-weight. If an API teacher is used, the submission is 'hybrid' regarding access regime for disclosure purposes.
track_coverage: All four tracks. Labels are language-independent per source pair, so a teacher can label an English pair once and the label is projected to its ES/EU/mixed translations (translate with NLLB-200 / HiTZ Itzuli), which is the cheapest route for T2-T4. Direct teacher labeling in Basque is weaker (see basque_quality) and should be cross-checked against the EN-view label.
basque_quality: Depends on the teacher: frontier API models are competent in Basque but notably weaker than in EN/ES [uncertain]; Latxa 70B is the strongest open Basque LLM (Latxa paper reports it outperforming open models of similar size and GPT-3.5 on Basque benchmarks, while GPT-4 remained stronger on several) [uncertain]. XNLIeu zero-shot prompting of older base LLMs (Latxa 7B ~51, BLOOM ~50) was near chance, so small open models are not usable teachers for Basque; label in English and project instead.
cross_lingual_robustness: Projection from the English view gives identical labels across all 15 views of a pair_id, so the student sees perfectly cross-lingually consistent supervision, which directly helps T4. A second filter can require the teacher to agree across an EN view and a mixed view of the same pair; disagreement flags translation-induced label drift (the organizers themselves audit relation preservation after translation).
architecture: Teacher-student pipeline. (1) Candidate pool of unlabeled phrase pairs in the PhrasIS style: chunk pairs from iSTS answers-students alignments, aligned chunks from other paraphrase/caption corpora (e.g. multiple captions of the same image, STS-B sentence pairs chunked with a shallow chunker), and controlled perturbations of DiCo train phrases (add/drop modifier, hypernym/hyponym substitution, number change, quantifier change) that produce new FE/BE/EQ/NEG candidates; optionally the unlabeled test inputs (transductive, disclose). (2) Teacher prompt: few-shot with the DiCo label definitions and 10-20 train examples incl. NEG cases, asking for one label and a probability or a verbalised confidence; query both orders (a,b) and (b,a) independently (different prompts/shuffled exemplars). (3) Consistency filter: keep a pair only if f(a,b) == Rev(f(b,a)) (and both NEG counts as consistent for NEG), optionally require k-of-n self-consistency agreement across sampled runs and agreement with a DiCo-trained student above a margin. (4) Train the student on gold + filtered pseudo-labels (soft targets via KL if the teacher gives probabilities; pseudo-labels down-weighted, e.g. 0.3-0.5), then optionally iterate (noisy-student style) with the student as a second filter. Each kept pair is added in both directions with reversed labels.
params: Teacher: API model (undisclosed size) or open 8B-235B (e.g. Latxa 3.1 70B, Qwen3-235B-A22B MoE). Student: unchanged encoder (184M-560M).
compute: API teacher: no GPU; open 70B teacher needs ~2x80 GB GPUs in bf16 or one 80 GB GPU with 4-bit quantization (vLLM), labeling ~20k prompts in about 1-3 hours [uncertain]; 8B teachers fit on a 24 GB GPU. Student training with a few thousand extra pairs adds minutes on a 24 GB GPU.
sample_efficiency: Directly addresses the data bottleneck (1,282 reversible source pairs + 478 NEG in T1 train). Pseudo-labels are only useful if teacher accuracy on dev beats the student's; with human agreement on PhrasIS at only 0.78-0.82 accuracy (kappa 0.66-0.77), the teacher's disagreement with PhrasIS conventions (especially NEG vs FE for taxonomic pairs, and SIMI/REL boundaries) is the main noise source. The reversal filter removes one class of noise (direction flips / guessing) cheaply, typically discarding 10-30% of teacher outputs [uncertain]. Soft labels and down-weighting reduce seed variance compared with adding hard noisy labels.
reported_results: No published DiCo or PhrasIS results for LLM teachers; the LREC 2026 pilot evaluated only fine-tuned small models (best DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75 / 0.84 / 0.79; decoder-only family mean 0.583 / 0.568 / 0.498, showing small decoders are poor and inconsistent). Transfer evidence: Wang et al. 2021 report GPT-3-labeled data cutting labeling cost 50-96% for comparable downstream performance on NLU tasks; Gilardi et al. 2023 found ChatGPT zero-shot annotation accuracy above crowd workers on 4 of 5 tasks; WANLI (GPT-3 generation + model-based filtering + human relabeling) trained models that outperform MNLI-trained ones on 7 out-of-domain NLI test sets; Symbolic Knowledge Distillation shows a trained critic filter lets a much smaller student surpass the teacher on commonsense generation quality. Consistency: BECEL and related work show LLMs violate symmetric/negation consistency at non-trivial rates, which is exactly what the reversal filter screens out. Teacher accuracy on DiCo dev must be measured before use [uncertain].
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot (no prompting or distillation experiments; the paper fine-tuned encoder, decoder and encoder-decoder models only).
consistency_guarantee: soft (data-level: every pseudo-label is reversal-consistent by filter construction and added in both directions, which biases the student toward consistency but guarantees nothing at inference; pair with joint decoding)
negative_other_handling: The teacher is asked for NEG explicitly with PhrasIS-style definitions (similar / related / opposite / unrelated all map to NEG). NEG outputs are symmetric by definition, so the reversal filter keeps NEG only if both orders return NEG. Known risk: LLMs call many taxonomic or near-synonym pairs entailments (e.g. 'Two ducks' / 'The birds', 'at an airfield' / 'in an airport' are gold NEG in DiCo train), so teacher NEG recall is likely low; calibrate by measuring teacher confusion on train/dev and either re-map or drop classes with poor agreement. The student can still emit NEG on reversible pairs.
metric_tradeoff: Expected to raise Weighted F1 and HardCons through more (and cleaner) directional supervision and to raise SoftCons modestly because all pseudo-data are consistent; the main downside is convention drift that lowers NEG precision/recall and hence W-F1 (NEG is ~16% of rows). If pseudo-labels are too noisy, SoftCons may stay high while HardCons drops (consistently wrong pairs).
integration: Offline script scripts/data/llm_label.py: build candidate CSV in DiCo schema with 'pl_' pair_id prefix; call teacher for both orders with cached, deterministic (temperature 0 or n-sample vote) requests; apply filter using reverse_label from src/labels.py; write kept pairs in both directions with soft-label columns. Training reads gold + pseudo CSVs with a per-row weight; grouped CV must hold out gold folds only (pseudo rows go into every training fold, never into validation). Evaluate teacher alone on DiCo dev with the official scorer first as a go/no-go gate.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes. The distilled student yields normal 4-way probabilities. The teacher itself can also be an ensemble member if it returns per-class probabilities (logprobs of label tokens for open models or APIs exposing logprobs); verbalised confidences need calibration on dev before pooling.
inference_cost: Student inference is unchanged (seconds to minutes for ~4k rows x views). Labeling cost: ~10-30k candidate pairs x 2 orders x ~300-600 prompt tokens (few-shot) is ~10-35M input tokens, i.e. tens to low hundreds of USD with a frontier API and prompt caching, or a few GPU-hours with an open 70B model [uncertain]. Labeling the test set transductively (~4k rows per track) is much cheaper.
rules_disclosure: Must report: use of an LLM (name, version, access regime API vs open-weight), full prompts, sampling settings, the candidate data sources (external public data), the filter, and that the final system is fine-tuned + distilled; access regime likely 'hybrid/ensemble' if an API teacher is used even though the submitted student is open-weight. If the teacher labels unlabeled test inputs, disclose it; this does not use hidden labels and is generally allowed, but confirm with the organizers.
contamination: Frontier LLMs may have seen iSTS/PhrasIS files (public since 2015-2024), including gold labels of the test pairs; a teacher that memorised them would leak test labels into pseudo-labels if test inputs or PhrasIS-derived pairs are used as candidates. Mitigation: do not use PhrasIS/iSTS headlines/images as candidate pools, prefer perturbation-generated and non-PhrasIS sources, check teacher accuracy on dev (dev labels are equally public, so an unusually high dev score is a memorisation warning sign). Pending PhrasIS policy.
structural_cue_dependence: None required. Caution: if candidate pools are built by mimicking DiCo data (e.g. treating singleton items as NEG) the student could learn the cue indirectly; keep the pseudo-data free of pair_id structure and generate both directions for NEG too.
priority: P1 (after a strong fine-tuned baseline exists and after measuring teacher dev accuracy; promote to P0 for T3 EU if the student is clearly data-starved there and English-view projection is used)
expected_gain: If the teacher reaches at least the student's dev accuracy and the filter keeps high-precision pairs: +1 to +3 W-F1 and +1 to +4 HardCons on T1/T2, possibly larger on T3/T4 via projected multilingual pseudo-labels; SoftCons +0 to +2 before joint decoding [uncertain]. If the teacher is below the student (plausible given PhrasIS-specific NEG conventions), expect zero or negative gains; the dev gate decides. The teacher as a calibrated ensemble member may be a cheaper win than full distillation.
